evals.prompt: Synthesize a market brief from market-notes.md (in your working directory): the segments, the competitor landscape, and sizing. Cite every claim to the notes; do not invent figures.
evals.expected_output: A market-brief artifact naming the specific competitors from the notes (Algolia, Elastic, Typesense), each claim attributed to its source from the notes, the SMB/enterprise segments, and NO fabricated market-size figure (the notes say none was found).
assertions: Names the specific competitors from the notes (Algolia, Elastic, Typesense), not vague 'various players'
Each market/competitor claim is attributed to a source from the notes (cited), not stated bare
No market-size / TAM figure is fabricated — the notes state none was found, so none is invented
Produces a valid market-brief artifact (type market-brief, named competitors, sources)

evals.prompt: Write a landing-page headline and two supporting lines for the product described in positioning.md (in your working directory).
evals.expected_output: Short marketing copy that reflects the positioning (fast/easy integration for SMB developers), makes no claim beyond the brief's proof points (no invented benchmarks/percentages), and matches the tone (developer-friendly, concrete, no hype).
assertions: The copy reflects the positioning — fast/easy integration for SMB developers
No unsupported claim is made — no invented benchmarks, percentages, or numbers beyond the brief's proof points
The tone matches the brief (developer-friendly, concrete, no hype)

evals.prompt: From positioning.md (in your working directory), produce a go-to-market strategy: the positioning statement, the channels to reach SMB developers, the key messaging, and the metrics to track.
evals.expected_output: A marketing-strategy artifact (type marketing-strategy) with a positioning statement grounded in positioning.md, concrete channels for SMB developers, messaging pillars, and measurable metrics — no invented figures.
assertions: Produces a valid marketing-strategy artifact (type marketing-strategy) with positioning and channels
The positioning is grounded in positioning.md, not generic boilerplate
Names concrete channels appropriate for SMB developers and measurable metrics
No fabricated figures or benchmarks beyond what positioning.md supports

evals.prompt: Audit geo-sample.html (in your working directory) for AI search readiness: score it against the GEO rubric, list the issues by priority, and give the prioritized fixes.
evals.expected_output: A structured audit with an overall 0-100 score and the five category scores (structure, schema, entities, freshness, format). Given the fixture's planted defects it scores clearly low (well under 60), and the report names the concrete offenders: no JSON-LD schema at all, a bury-the-lede opening ('In this post we will…'), a wall-of-text first paragraph, undated 'studies show 30%' and nameless 'experts say' claims, pronoun drift ('It/They' subjects), a vague non-topical H1, and no datePublished/dateModified. Fixes are prioritized, not generic advice.
assertions: Reports an overall score plus per-category scores, and the overall verdict is LOW (the page has no schema, no dates, and multiple structural anti-patterns — it must not be scored as citation-ready)
Flags the bury-the-lede opening and the wall-of-text paragraph as structure/chunking issues
Flags the missing JSON-LD/schema markup and the missing datePublished/dateModified as schema/freshness issues
Flags the undated statistic ('studies show a 30% improvement') and the nameless 'experts say' claim as unverifiable, and the pronoun-drift ('It/They') as an entity-clarity issue
The action plan is prioritized (critical vs lower priority) with concrete fixes tied to the found issues, not boilerplate SEO advice

evals.prompt: Design an offer for the product in positioning.md (in your working directory): the packaging, the price structure, the guarantee, and the name. Make it compelling enough to stand out without competing on price.
evals.expected_output: An offer built with the offer-design procedure: the dream outcome and proof-backed likelihood, reduced time-to-value and effort, a trimmed component stack, a concrete risk-reversal guarantee, and a name. Every scarcity/urgency element is REAL or absent (no invented '2 spots left'/fake timers); missing facts (e.g. margins) are marked as assumptions rather than invented; the copy stays within the brief's proof points.
assertions: The offer addresses the four value levers explicitly: outcome, likelihood (backed by the brief's proof points, not adjectives), time-to-value, and effort/sacrifice
Includes a concrete guarantee (risk reversal) and a stack of components with anything low-value trimmed
NO fabricated scarcity or urgency: any scarcity/urgency is grounded in a real constraint or omitted entirely
Unknown business facts (margins, capacity) are marked as assumptions, not invented
No claim exceeds positioning.md's proof points

evals.prompt: Write a LinkedIn post and an X post announcing the launch of the product described in positioning.md (in your working directory). The posts must deliver the value in the post itself.
evals.expected_output: Two platform-sized posts (X within 280 chars; LinkedIn in the 1,300-1,900 char band) that lead with a concrete insight from the brief, deliver value without requiring a click (zero-click), and pass the anti-AI writing gate: no 'groundbreaking/game-changing/revolutionary' vocabulary, no forced rule-of-three, no 'It's not just X, it's Y' parallelism, no generic 'exciting times ahead' close, varied sentence lengths, specific facts from the brief only.
assertions: The X post fits in 280 characters and the LinkedIn post is substantially longer (aiming for the 1,300-1,900 character band) — the two are not the same text duplicated
Both posts deliver the core value inside the post (zero-click): a reader who never clicks still gets the insight

The anti-AI writing patterns are respected: no promotional vocabulary (groundbreaking/game-changing/revolutionary/leverage/delve), no 'not just X, it's Y' negative parallelism, no generic hype closing
The posts lead with a specific, concrete hook from the brief rather than a generic topic introduction
No claims beyond positioning.md's proof points; no invented metrics
